findings.title: CVE-2026-7644: improper authorization in NextChat addMcpServer
findings.summary_md: VulDB published CVE-2026-7644 for an improper authorization flaw in ChatGPTNextWeb NextChat up to v2.16.1 in the addMcpServer function of app/mcp/actions.ts; remote exploitation is possible and an exploit was disclosed publicly. The entry was reserved on 2026-05-01 and published on 2026-05-02. This is the vulnerability Zeabur later identified as the entry point for its August 2026 breach.

findings.title: Zeabur August 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: On August 27, 2026 an attacker exploited CVE-2026-7644 in a customer's NextChat v2.16.1 service on a shared cluster and escalated through four system boundaries to AWS root access and the production database, reading account information and project environment variables. Zeabur sent user notices on August 28 at 08:53 and 17:03 UTC, disabled all Legacy API Keys, rotated internal credentials, disconnected the shared cluster from production, and published remediation guidance. The incident affected project environment variables holding third-party API keys, cloud credentials, database passwords, and other secrets.

findings.title: Zeabur Discloses Second Breach in Seven Weeks, Exposing API Tokens
findings.summary_md: TokenPost reported that Zeabur disclosed a second breach in less than seven weeks, with attackers accessing user secrets and some user-rented dedicated servers on Google Cloud. Exposed data included environment variables, account details, Zeabur API tokens, and zSend email service keys, with the intrusion window placed at October 14, 13:00-17:00 UTC. Zeabur urged users to sign in again, replace stored secrets, create new API tokens, and reset root passwords on affected dedicated servers.

findings.title: Zeabur is shutting down: what happens next
findings.summary_md: Zeabur's founder announced the platform will wind down, with shared cluster services pausing on December 1, 2026 and all dedicated servers and shared clusters stopping by December 31, 2026. The post attributed the decision to a second security incident on October 14, 2026 UTC with broader scope than the August incident, alongside scaling complexity after three and a half years of growth. Purchases of new dedicated servers and domains stopped immediately and renewal was disabled.

findings.title: Zeabur Is Shutting Down: A Taiwanese Startup's Growing Pains
findings.summary_md: A developer blog analyzing Zeabur's shutdown described the August breach entry point as an authorization flaw in a customer's NextChat MCP feature and lateral movement through poorly isolated internal systems. It also covered the October breach and the wind-down timeline. The post was published on October 18, 2026.

findings.title: Zeabur October 2026 security incident (preliminary report)
findings.summary_md: Zeabur's preliminary report states that on October 14-15, 2026 an attacker used leaked plaintext internal credentials to access shared clusters across nine regions, some Dedicated Servers, and Zeabur internal systems, then read the platform database. The incident affected 321,810 accounts and roughly 3.2 million environment-variable records, with root sign-ins on 101 GCP servers. Admin tokens had no expiry, were created in January 2024, and were not included in the post-August rotation.
